source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately reporting failed municipal water-quality tests to protect the public

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Identify the water samples that have failed to meet state and federal requirements.
3. Record the specific parameters (eg. coliform bacteria, lead levels) that fell short of the required quality standards.
4. Document the location of the affected water supply system.
5. Note the date(s) and time(s) of sample collection.
6. Include the test methods used.
7. Specify the acceptable range of each tested parameter and the actual results that caused the failure.
8. Describe any immediate action taken, such as issuing a boil water advisory.
9. Report the potential health consequences of consuming the contaminated water.
10. Outline any follow-up testing and mitigation efforts planned or underway.

11. Prepare a public statement or notification.
12. Summarize the situation succinctly: where, when, which contaminants were detected.
13. Clearly explain what the failure means (e.g., boil water order) in non-technical terms.
14. State any immediate actions
